non_goals: Implementing any capability generation, planning, or apply behavior.
Removing or rewriting any part of the existing Item application.
Creating the repoctl package or any repository-generation domain code.
Introducing the capability lifecycle states or derived index compilation.
epic_contract.outcome: A generated repository classifies every one of its paths into exactly one of four disjoint ownership zones, and the pack proves mechanically that a foundation update can never write a product path.
success_metrics: Every path in a freshly generated repository resolves to exactly one of FOUNDATION, PRODUCT, DERIVED, DECLARATION, and an unclassified path fails the generated gate.
A pack test fails when any tracked path under template/ resolves to a PRODUCT root.
A synthetic foundation-version-B update leaves every hand-seeded product file byte-identical.
One structural capability validator accepts both a system capability root and a product capability root with no rule weakened for the system root.
Adding a file under template/ requires editing no recorded constant, so two template changes to different files never contend on the same line.

children.goal: The whole-tree digest assertion is removed, so several template changes can land without contending on one recorded constant.
The zone vocabulary and the declaration and derived layout are stated once, as data, with a pure classifier over them.
Every claim the zone table makes is enforced by a check that fails on a real violation rather than documented in prose.
One root table names four disjoint zones; the layout those zones describe exists in a generated repository.
The proof surface becomes a multi-catalog tree with one policy, so a capability outside src/ can own properties later without a second engine.
One structural validator serves system and product capability roots, with no rule weakened for the system root.
The replacing specification and ADR are landed as the repository's dated decision record.

goal_tree.goal: Ownership is a mechanically decided property of every path, and the pack can prove product code is unreachable from a foundation update.

acceptance_criteria: In a generated repository, `uv run python -m scripts.capability_validator --root <fixture-capability>` exits 0 for a well-formed capability and non-zero for each of: missing api.py, missing domain/, domain importing application, and an external module importing capability internals.
The validator is invoked twice in a test with different root and ownership parameters, and a test asserts the two invocations resolve to the same rule identifier set.
A test fails if any rule is disabled, softened, or skipped for a system capability root.
`uv run python scripts/quality_gate.py` still passes on the unchanged generated repository.
capability_structural_validator.decision_boundary: Owns the validator's parameterization, its rule identifiers, and how capability roots are discovered. May not create any capability, may not change the existing ARCH rule numbering for non-capability code, and may not grant the system root an exemption.
capability_structural_validator.outcome: One parameterized validator checks required structure, layer direction, and the api.py-only public surface for any capability root, and refuses to run with a weakened rule set for a system root.

acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn EXPECTED_GENERATED_TREE_SHA256 .` returns no match in the tracked tree.
`just test` and `just test-fast` both pass.
After adding a new file under template/, `just test-fast` passes with no edit to any test constant; the probe file is removed before the final commit.
The four variant-delta tests still run and still assert exact file-set deltas: `pytest -q tests/test_instantiate.py -k delta_or_identical` collects at least four tests and passes.
`just test-fast` still renders the complete default template and still runs the pin-coherence and hook-policy tests, asserted by reading the justfile recipe in a test.
drop_tree_digest.decision_boundary: Owns what `just test-fast` runs in place of the digest test. May not delete or weaken any variant-delta test, and may not replace the digest with another single recorded constant over the whole tree.
drop_tree_digest.outcome: The whole-tree digest assertion and its recorded constant are removed, so a template change no longer forces an edit to a shared line; the coverage that mattered stays in the runtime variant-delta tests.

acceptance_criteria: In a generated repository, `uv run python -m scripts.ownership_guard` exits 0 and prints the count of classified paths.
After editing the root table so two zone roots overlap, the guard exits non-zero and names both overlapping roots.
After adding a tracked file under a path matched by no root, the guard exits non-zero and names that path.
`uv run python scripts/quality_gate.py` runs the ownership guard, and removing it from the gate makes a pack test fail.
ownership_disjointness_guard.decision_boundary: Owns the guard's error codes, its message text, and its position in the gate order. May not change the zone table, the classifier signature, or add new zones.
ownership_disjointness_guard.outcome: The generated quality gate fails when two ownership roots overlap or when any tracked path resolves to no zone.

acceptance_criteria: A generated repository contains a single root table naming FOUNDATION, PRODUCT, DERIVED, and DECLARATION roots, and `grep -rn` finds no second definition of those roots in the generated tree.

In a generated repository, `uv run pytest tests/unit/scripts/test_ownership.py -q` passes and covers: a FOUNDATION path, a PRODUCT path, a DERIVED path, a DECLARATION path, an absolute path, and a path containing `..`.
The classifier returns exactly one zone for every path in the generated tree; the test enumerates the real tree rather than a fixture list.
The classifier rejects an absolute path and a `..` escape with a distinct, named error rather than returning a zone.
ownership_zones.decision_boundary: Owns the zone names, the root table's file format and location, and the classifier's signature and precedence rules. May not decide capability internal structure, the proof catalog layout, or CLI behavior.
ownership_zones.outcome: A generated repository states its four ownership zones once as data and resolves any repository-relative path to exactly one of them through a pure classifier.

acceptance_criteria: In a generated repository, `uv run python -m scripts.proof_guard` exits 0 and `uv run python -m scripts.proof_guard --report` lists exactly the same eight property IDs it listed before this change.
The generated repository contains proof/policy.toml and at least one catalog file; the single root proof.toml no longer exists.
`just test` passes with tests/test_proof_guard.py collected and green.
The loader rejects two catalogs declaring the same property ID with a named error, proven by a test.
The loader rejects a catalog whose declared ownership zone disagrees with its path, proven by a test.
`just prove` passes in the generated repository.
proof_catalog_multi_root.decision_boundary: Owns the catalog tree layout, the policy schema, the aggregation and ownership-metadata rules, and the generated index format. May not add, remove, or restate any existing property, and may not introduce a capability concept into the proof engine.
proof_catalog_multi_root.outcome: The proof surface is one policy plus N catalogs aggregated into a generated index, with the existing eight properties preserved unchanged and every existing proof check still green.

acceptance_criteria: A generated repository contains .repo/repository.toml with schema_version = 1, and `python -c` loading it with tomllib succeeds.
A generated repository contains an empty active-capability index, an empty composition index, an empty product CLI index, and proof/_generated/index.json.
Every derived file's first lines contain the generated banner and a source-state digest; a test asserts the banner on each derived file by reading the real tree.
The classifier from ownership-zones-v1 returns DERIVED for every path under the generated roots and DECLARATION for .repo/repository.toml; asserted by a test, not by prose.
`just validate` passes with these files present.
repository_declaration.decision_boundary: Owns the repository declaration's fields, the derived banner text, and the digest's input definition. May not decide capability declaration fields, lifecycle states, or how indexes are recompiled.
repository_declaration.outcome: A freshly generated repository ships a versioned repository declaration and empty derived indexes that carry a generated banner and a source-state digest.

acceptance_criteria: In a generated repository, `uv run python -m scripts.docs_guard` exits 0.
The new ADR carries the four required front-matter keys and a status drawn from the allowed set, and names the ADRs it supersedes.
docs/README.md registers every new document; adding an unregistered document makes the docs guard fail.
DESIGN_GUARDRAILS.md gains a row mapping the ownership-zone guard, the template product-root guard, and the capability validator to the design intent each enforces.
spec_and_adr.decision_boundary: Owns the ADR number, its wording, and which prior ADRs it supersedes. May not change any guard, script, or generated code, and may not restate a fact that a guard already checks.
spec_and_adr.outcome: The recursive proof-carrying repository specification and the ADR that supersedes the example-application decision are landed, registered, and link-checked.

acceptance_criteria: `just test` passes with tests/test_ownership_zones.py collected and green.
The test reads the PRODUCT root list from the same source the generated classifier reads; it does not hard-code a duplicate list, and a test asserts the two sources are the same file.
After adding a file at template/src/{{ package }}/modules/placeholder.py, the test fails and names that path.
The test covers the four PRODUCT roots named in the specification: product modules, proof modules, tests modules, and verification modules.
template_product_root_guard.decision_boundary: Owns this test's location and how it reads the PRODUCT root list. May not change the root list itself, and may not add an allowlist exception without the epic's ADR naming it.
template_product_root_guard.outcome: The pack fails its own test suite if any path under template/ would render into a PRODUCT root, so a scaffold update can never own product code.

acceptance_criteria: `just test` passes with tests/test_update_preservation.py collected and green.

The test renders foundation A, hand-seeds one capability from tests/fixtures/capability_seed/, modifies every seeded product file, applies a synthetic foundation B, regenerates derived indexes, and compares SHA-256 of every seeded product file before and after.
The comparison is byte-for-byte over every seeded product file, and the test fails when a deliberate mutation makes version B overwrite one seeded file.
The test asserts derived files did change across the update, proving the comparison is not vacuously green.
update_preservation_seeded.decision_boundary: Owns how the synthetic version-B foundation change is constructed and how the hand-seeded capability fixture is shaped. May not invoke capability generation, which does not exist in this epic, and may not relax the byte-for-byte requirement to a semantic comparison.
update_preservation_seeded.outcome: A synthetic foundation-version-B update over a repository whose seeded product files were all modified leaves every one of those files byte-identical.
